full_judgment:
Bhishmadev Chakrabortty J: This appeal at the instance of a convict is directed against the judgment and order dated 5-6-2008 passed by the Special Judge, Court No. 10, Dhaka in Special Case No. 1 of 2008 arising out of Uttara Police Station Case No. 76 dated 26-7-2007 corresponding to ACC GR No. 69 of 2007 convicting the appellant under sections 27 (1) of the Durnitee Daman Commission Ain, 2004 (in brief the Ain, 2004) and sentencing him thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 10 (ten) years with a fine of Taka 10 (ten) lac, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 1 (one) year more and further convicting and sentencing him under section 26(2) of the Ain, 2004 to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 (two) years to run concurrently and also confiscating the property as described in the said judgment.

2. By the same judgment the appellant's wife Mohsenara Goni (absconding) was also convicted under section 27(1) of the Ain, 2004 read with section 109 of the Penal Code and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 (three) years with a fine of Taka 1(one) lac, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6 (six) months more with an order of confiscation of her property.

3. PW 1 Golam Shahriar Chowdhury, a Deputy Director of Anti-Corruption Commission (in brief ACC) lodged a First Information Report (in brief the FIR) with Uttara Police Station on 6-7-2007 alleging, inter alia, that the appellant, in reply to a notice of the ACC issued under section 26 of the Ain, 2004, furnished his wealth statement showing movable and immovable property belonged him and his wife worth Taka 3,70,15,000 with 300 bhoris of gold ornaments. But on inquiry it was found that he suppressed wealth of Taka 54,81,590 in the wealth statement and asset of Taka 4,29,52,115.05 in his name and that of his wife which was disproportionate to his legal and known source of Income.

4. PW 54 SM Akhtar Hamid Bhuiyan, an Assistant Director of ACC investigated into the allegation and submitted a charge sheet being No. 446 dated 13-12-2007 against the appellant and his wife under sections 26(2), 27(1) of the Ain, 2004 read with section 109 of the Penal Code.

5. The record of the case, thereafter, was transmitted to the Court of Senior Special Judge, Dhaka and registered as Special Case No. 169 of 2007 who on 19-12-2007 took cognizance of offence under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Ain, 2004 and Rule 15 (gha) (5) of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007 read with section 109 of the Penal Code against the appellant and his wife.

6. Subsequently the case was transferred to the Special Judge, Court No. 10, Dhaka for trial and renumbered as Special Case No.1 of 2008. The Special Judge on 15-1-2008 framed charge against the appellant under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Ain, 2004 and his wife under the 27(1) of the Ain, 2004, read with section 109 of the Penal Code.

7. The prosecution examined as many as 54 (fifty four) witnesses, who were cross-examined by the defense. On conclusion of trial, the appellant was examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (briefly the Code), wherein he reiterated his innocence and examined 2 (two) defense witnesses including himself as DW 1.

8. The learned Special Judge, on conclusion of trial pronounced the judgment and order of conviction and sentence on 5-6-2004 as stated above.

9. Mr. M Sayed Ahmed, learned Advocate for the appellant takes us through the FIR, charge sheet, and the evidence on record and submits that the learned Special Judge failed to assess the evidence of the prosecution witnesses in their legal perspective in ascertaining the movable and immovable property of the appellant and that of his wife. Admittedly the appellant was arrested on 29-5-2007 from his house and after a along unauthorized police custody was sent to jail hajat, wherefrom a notice under section 26(1) of the Ain, 2004 for submitting wealth statement was served upon him giving seven days time and in response therewith he submitted the statement on 26-6-2007. He was not given enough time and opportunity to prepare the statement and it was prepared and submitted from recollection of his memory. The appellant did not conceal anything about his wealth in the statement. In the adverse situation prevailing at that time there might be some omission, which should be ignored in the interest of justice.

10. Mr Ahmed then submits that Taka 1,06,48,600 which was alleged to have been recovered from his house was shown in his wealth statement. The father-in-law of the appellant sworn an affidavit before the notary public at New York declaring that he gave approximately Taka 1,61,14,000 and gold ornaments to the appellant and his wife to purchase land, for construction of building etc. 125 bhoris of gold ornaments was also mentioned in the statement and shown in the tax return of 1990-91, out of which 25 bhoris were of his own. He received the rest from his mother-in-law, sister-in-law and brother-in-law. Taka 47,586 in the savings account and Taka 6,44,114 in account of fixed deposit in Janata Bank, Barisal Corporate Branch was duly shown in the return. Taka 20,321.88 in account No. 512 maintained with United Commercial Bank, Barisal Branch was also shown in the statement which was admitted by PW 46. Taka (5+5.10) 10 lac in another account of fixed deposit maintained with Standard Charter Bank has been proved by PW 43. Savings Certificate of Taka 1,11,500 in Patuakhali post office, furniture of his residence worth Taka 2,21,000 and electronic goods of Taka 7,05,600 was mentioned in his wealth statement. 7.5 kathas of land belongs to the appellant at Purbachal, Sector- 2, as stated in the statement has also been admitted by PW 50; 5 kathas of land of sector- 10, Uttara is yet to be partitioned; 1762 square feet of land in the name of Mohsenara and her mother; a six storied building at 96/4/B Moneswar Road, Jigatola, were yet to be partitioned, also mentioned and shown in his tax return. The Commission did not issue any notice upon his wife, father-in-law and brother-in-law. The Investigating Officer did not investigate into the original ownership of the ornaments. PW 8 admitted in the cross-examination that he had no warrant with him at the time of raiding the appellant's houses. Them was no provision to inquire the cases of ACC by the police, but the Investigating Officer made inquiry by the police and the police within a day inquired the 50 addresses of the relatives of his wife, which was absurd and not believable. The appellant in the wealth statement gave the approximate value of his properties, but the 10 treated the same as untrue. It was impossible for him to write the correct figure in his statement of wealth from inside the Jail. The income tax returns were not submitted as evidence during trial. The informant admitted in his evidence that the appellant told him that he obtained the property from his father-in-law. His wife failed to show any documents as the law enforcing agency took all the documents at the time of raiding his house. The Investigating Officer did not visit all the places where the convict served. Some materials were seized from his house on the basis of a GD entry and subsequently the case was filed by the ACC, and, as such, the alamots and seized articles cannot be taken into consideration as prosecution materials according to the provisions of law. Relying on the cases of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Shamima Begum, 60 DLR (AD) 277; Anti-Corruption Commission vs Nargis Begum, 62 DLR (AD) 279 and the Anti-Corruption Commission vs Mohiuddin Khan Alomgir, 62 DLR (AD) 290, Mr Ahmed further submits that a notice must allow a reasonable time to check-up the details of the assets of a person, if necessary, on examination of his records and after consultation with his lawyers and others concerned persons. Section 26 certainly does not envisage a notice upon a person who is in detention. The person concerned most be afforded a fair and reasonable opportunity to respond to the notice, otherwise, it is no notice in the eye of law. A notice under section 26 of the Ain, 2004 to a detenu away from his hearth and home, cannot be said to be fair and bonafide exercise of power. By pointing out the evidence of some prosecution witnesses, the learned Advocate submits that the prosecution by adducing the oral and documentary evidence failed to prove the charge against the appellant beyond all reasonable doubt, and, as such, he is entitled to be acquitted.

11. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate appearing for the ACC submits that although the notice was sewed upon the appellant inside the jail, it has already been settled by our Apex Court that a person can be served with a notice even inside the jail and there is no bar in serving such a notice. Law gives 7 days time for submitting statement of wealth which can be extended for a further period of 7 days according to the provisions of rule 17 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 (in brief the Rules, 2007). The evidence of DW 1, the appellant, does not show that he was not in a position to furnish a fully correct statement. The appellant also did not take such defence that due to his detainment he failed to submit the statement correctly. The trial Court on consideration of the materials on record and the evidence both oral and documentary found that the appellant had concealed huge property both movable and immovable in his statement, which also was disproportionate to his known and legal source of income. The wife of the appellant being a house wife cannot be the owner of the wealth as found. The appellant hopelessly failed to show that he and his wife got those properties from other sources. The appellant tried to explain that those were obtained from other sources, but failed to establish it. The learned Special Judge on correct assessment of evidence and proposition of law and fact passed the impugned judgment convicting and sentencing the appellant and his wife and confiscating the property. There is nothing on record to interfere with the judgment and order of conviction and sentence, and, as such, the appeal would be dismissed. In view of the above submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides, let us examine the evidence on record.

12. PW 1 Gholam Shaharier Chowdhury, a Deputy Director of ACC and the informant, deposed that by Exhibit-1 dated 7-6-2007 he was permitted to do preliminary inquiry against accused. Osman Goni of acquiring wealth by corruption and misusing of power. By Exhibit-2 dated 12-6-2007, Osman Goni was directed to submit wealth statement of him and his wife and other dependents and by Exhibit-3 dated 26-6-2007 the appellant submitted the statement. The ACC on preliminary inquiry by its report dated 17-7-2007 found the movable and immovable property of Taka 1,28,87,500 of him against the statement of Taka 1,22,50,000 submitted by him. In the said statement 1762 square feet of land at Jigatola received by his wife Mohsenara Goni from her mother, 0.2424 acres of land of Dakshin Khan and 3 Kathas of Sector-13, Uttara received by his wife from her father was suppressed. The ACC found movable property of them valuing Taka 3,19,05,144.05 wherein the appellant made declaration of Taka 2,47,65,000 along with 300 bhories of gold ornaments. He acquired moveable property of Taka 3,19,05,144.05 which includes the value of 300 bhories of gold of Taka 22,96,054 + cash Taka 1,06,81,500 (seized by the police from his house) + savings certificate of Taka 32,11,500 which includes saving certificate of Taka 27,00,000 seized by police. Taka 1,50,41,090.15 maintained with the bank includes FDR of Taka 11,00,000 seized by the police and GPF fund of Taka 6,75,000 including the money recovered from his house of 'Banobithi from inside a drum of rice, cover of pillows, suitcase, FDR and savings certificates.

13. During inquiry on the statement of immovable property of 5 kathas of land of Sector-10, Uttara valuing Taka 30,00,000, 1762 square feet of land of Moneswar Road valuing Taka 1,85,000, 5 storied building on his purchased land including construction cost of Taka 80,90,000, 0.06 acres of land valuing Taka 3,00,000/- purchased in the name of Mohsenara Goni and 71/2 kathas of land of Sector-2, Purbachal in the name of appellant for which Taka 13,12,500 was deposited to Rajuk, i.e., totally of 1,28,81,500 takas movable 'and immovable property. The Commission found their wealth of Taka 4,47,92,644.05 on verification and inspection. He further stated that the accused in the statement of wealth described that they got those from his father-in-law, but his wife on interrogation failed to show deeds and papers in support of those. If the value of 300 bhories of gold be of Taka 22,96,054, the value of his wealth stands at Taka 4,24,96,590.05 except the gold, but he disclosed the same at Taka 3,70,15,000 and thus suppressed wealth of Taka 54,81,590.05. He further deposed that the accused during his service tenure withdrew Taka 28,48,650.92 as salary and others. During inquiry it was found from his tax return that he had shown his total wealth of Taka 16,93,039. From the TIN number of his wife it was found that she submitted income tax return in 1990-91 for the first time and showed that she had got Taka 1,85,000 from each of his 50 relatives as donation on 30 June 1991. In the enquiry the addresses of those 50 persons were found false and fake. The officer found cinema hall and electricity office in the given addresses and submitted the report as above. Mohsenara Goni also failed to provide any information about those donors which proves the story of donation as false. In the tax return she also showed US$ 19,000 equivalent to Taka 6,08,000 as gift, but no such document was found in the income tax file. She also failed to show anything in support of so called donation for which statement of wealth of Taka 98,58,000 as above was proved to be of false. In the income tax file Taka 80,90,000 was shown as construction cost of the building at Moneswar Road and the value of 5 kathas of land in Sector-10, Uttara at Taka 15,25,000 was expensed form the money of donation or gift, Taka 18,13,780 received as house rent shown in the tax return of 2006-07, was obtained from the income of his illegal assets. In the tax return of 1990.91, the value of her ornament was shown at Taka 50,000 and the present value of those stands at Taka 1,37,020. Except the value of furniture of Take 16,43,039 the total value of his assets stood at Take 17,03,509 which could be considered to be from his legal income. In the tax return of 2006-07 Mohsenara Gerd showed the value of his ornaments at Taka 50,000, which stands now at Taka 1,03,728 and, as such, the total value of their asset was at Taka 18,40,529. He disclosed the total value of the movable and immovable property of him and his family members at Taka 4,47,92,644.05 except electronic goods and furniture and, as such, she acquired wealth of Take (4,47,92,644.05 18,40,529) = 4,29,5,215.15 illegally in their names which was beyond his legal and known sources of income. He also suppressed wealth of Taka 54,81,590.05 in his wealth statement. After preliminary inquiry he found the above allegation to be true and according sanction from the ACC lodged the FIR, Exhibit- 5.

14. In the cross-examination he stated that during inquiry the appellant was inside the jail. He did not know the reason for detainment of the accused. He considered Exhibit-3 the statement of assets and the explanation of the accused He also interrogated other people at the time of inquiry. He collected the banks statements of the accused, but did not find anything about foreign currency or remittance. He denied the suggestion that the accused had no property beyond the statement and the acquired wealth was kept in his name and in the name of his wife. He denied the suggestion that in order to harass the accused the FIR was lodged on false averments. He also denied that no occurrence took place in the house at 'Banobithi and the submitted returns from 1979 to 2007 were correct; that the accused committed no offence and nothing was acquired by illegal means, or that without inquiring and verifying the statement of wealth the FIR was lodged.

15. PW 2 Rina Sana, a Sub-Inspector of police, deposed that on 26-7-2007 while she was serving in Uttara Model Police Station received the written FIR, filled up the form and registered the case. She proved the FIR form Exhibit-7, her signature- 7/1. In the cross-examination she stated that in the FIR the date and time of occurrence was mentioned as 1979 to 27-6-2007, but no date of 1979 was mentioned. Nothing was mentioned in the FIR as to the cause of delay in lodging it. She received the FIR from the informant through constable Alauddin of ACC. She did not mention anything in the form about the CC. In the FIR form she wrote date 27-7-2007 and showed the place of occurrence as Banobithi, building-1, 3rd floor, Sector-8, Uttara, Dhaka.

16. PW 3 Md. Golani Haidar, the Senior Jail Super, Dhaka Central Jail, deposed that on 27-6-2007 by memo No. 9342 he sent the wealth statement furnished by accused Osman Coni to the Secretary of ACC. He proved the forwarding letter Exhibit-3, his signature-3/1. In the cross-examination he stated that on 26-6-2007 accused Osman Goni sent the wealth statement to him from inside the jail. He knew the accused from the date of his entrance into the jail. The accused on 18-6-2007 got the notice from the ACC to submit the statement.

17. PW 4 Md. Shamsur Rahman, a Conservator of Forest, deposed that he prepared the salary statement of the accused from October, 1979 to May, 2007 showing withdrawal of Taka 28,48,650.92 as salary and others. He sent the statement to the Director of ACC on 12-5-2007. He proved the statement Exhibit-8, his signature- 8/1. In the cross-examination he replied that in the said salary statement the amount withdrawn by the accused was shown. He failed to state as to whether there was any allegation against the accused in his office. The accused went aboard for several times, but he failed to state the numbers. The salary withdrawn by the accused while he was abroad was mentioned in the statement.

In the cross-examination he denied the suggestion that he did not put his signature on the seizure list.

29. PW 16 Md. Sharif Miah, an employee of IK Jewellers Uttara, deposed that on 29-5-2007 the police recovered and seized 135 bhoris of gold ornaments from accused's house and he took weight of those by electronic machine. He proved the seizure list and identified his signature- 13/4. He also proved the materials produced before the court. In the cross-examination he, replied that he took weight of the ornaments along with stone. He replied that he was present at the time of preparing seizure list.

30. PW 17 Mousumi Barman, an Assistant Commissioner of Taxes, Tax Zone-4, Dhaka deposed that on 20-8-2007 SM Akhter Hamid Bhuiyan of ACC, seized the income tax files of accused Osman Goni from 1993-94 to 2006-07. The seized files were government records which could be inspected locally. He also replied that the fixation of tax was made according to the prevailing law,

74. Let us examine whether the appellant had suppressed his wealth in the statement ?

75. The Anti-Corruption Commission on inquiry and scrutiny of the statement submitted by the appellant found concealment and discrepancy and also found huge wealth beyond his known and legal source of income. Than a regular case was filed after according sanction from the Commission and PW 54 was appointed as Investigating Officer. During investigation PW 54 collected evidence, seized alamats, recorded statements under section 161 of the Code and submitted the charge sheet obtaining sanction from the Commission.

76. The allegation against the appellant was that he suppressed wealth of Taka 1,02,53,584.47 in his wealth statement. Being a government servant he also illegally acquired wealth of Taka 4,96,81,464.31, which was beyond his known and legal source of income.

77. Appellant Osman Goni did not show Taka 6,44,114 kept against fixed deposit No. 419533/2036 in Janata Bank, Corporate Branch, Barisal in his wealth statement and the said deposit has been proved by PWs 18 and 19, two officers of the said bank. Seizure list of the same has been proved as Exhibit-17 and documents as Material Exhibit-VII. The said amount was not denied by the appellant in the cross-examination of those PWs. The appellant in the wealth statement did also not show the amount of Taka 3,05,766.02 kept against Savings Account No. 181571648/01 in Standard Chartered Bank, Khulna Branch, which was substantiated by the evidence of PW 54, the investigating officer vide seizure list, Exhibit-21 and Material Exhibit-XI The amount was subsequently transferred from the account of Osman Goni to the joint account in their name. PW 27 proved the said joint account. The same was also not denied by the appellant in the cross-examination. The other materials recovered from the house of the appellant worth Taka 7,05,600 was proved by PW 38 AKM Ruhul Amin a 1st Class Magistrate, PW 45 Sree Gopal Chandra Roy, PW 54 the investigating officer, PW 48 Bidip Ranjan Saha Roy, PW 49 Md. Abdul Mannan and PW 47 Md. Shakhawat Hossain and by Exhibit-29. But no specific suggestion was put to those witnesses that he was not the owner of those articles. The appellant also did not mention the value of those goods in his wealth statement and thus suppressed it. The value of the furniture of his houses was ascertained at Taka 2,21,000 and has been proved by PW 35 Md. Ahsan Aziz and PW 36 Kazi Mahbubul Hoque and they were not challenged to that effect by the defense. Thus the appellant also suppressed the value of the furniture. Although he mentioned in his wealth statement that he had Taka 1 (one) crore in his home but it has been proved by the evidence of PW 8 Md. Mijanur Rahaman a sub-Inspector, PW 11 Md. Ashrafuzzaman, PW 9 Md. Masudur Rahman and Exhibit-14 and Material Exhibit-IV that they recovered cash Taka 1,06,84,600 in total from his house and thus he suppressed Taka 6,84,600 in his statement. In addition he suppressed some other Bank statements regarding his wealth maintained in different banks in Dhaka, Barisal and Khulna. In view of the above, the prosecution has been able to prove that the appellant suppressed wealth of Taka 1,02,53,584.87 in his statement for which he is liable to be convicted under section 26(2) of the Ain, 2004.

78. Let us see whether the prosecution has been able to prove that the appellant acquired wealth beyond his legal source of income. It is already found that Taka 1,06,84,600 was seized and recovered from the house of the appellant. He failed to show any reasonable and acceptable explanation about the source of such huge money. Although he disclosed that the money so recovered was his own money, but no such declaration was made in his income tax return. The appellant in his statement of wealth disclosed that the house on 5 kathas of land at Moneswar Road was purchased in the name of his wife and mother-in-law at the cost of Taka 12 lac and the estimated value of the building was at Taka 50 lac, but the prosecution by the evidence of PW 13 proved the seized docu Ment Exhibit-40 and found the value of it at Taka 1,50,000 purchased by his mother-in-law and gifted it to accused Mohsenara Goni. In the income tax return the total value of it was shown as Taka 62,00,000 but the concerned engineers, i.e., PWs 41 and 42 ascertained the value of it at Taka 1,01,17,793 out of which 50% was gifted to Mohsenara was valid, but remaining 50% of the same was not donated to her as evident from Exhibit-40 and Material Exhibit-XVIII which has been proved by the evidence of PW 13 and the some was not denied by the appellant by cross-examination, and, as such, the gift of 50% from his mother-in-law was false. According to the income tax file of accused Mohsenara Goni Exhibit-10, proved by PW 25 Shahjahan Ali, Additional Assistant Commissioner of Taxes, she received gift from 50 persons, Taka 1,85,000 from each, i.e., totally of Taka 92,50,000 and US $ 19000, but in the enquiry the story of gift was found false. PW 7 SI Kamruuaman verified the addresses and found no existence of the persons and submitted the report vide Exhibit-10. The value ascertained by the engineers of the concerned department was at the scheduled rate applicable for the relevant time, which cannot be disbelieved without any contrary evidence and, as such, the cost of construction and the value of land amounting to Taka 1,03,17,793 is also beyond his legal source of income. The investigating officer also recovered 155 bhoris of gold from the locker of Standard Chartered Bank, out of which the appellant showed in his income tax return Taka 40,000, which is equivalent to the value of 20 bhoris, but failed to show the source of the ornaments of remaining 270 bhoris, and, as such, those are also beyond his legal source of income. The prosecution by the evidence of PWs 8,12 and 13 proved the value of the gold as ascertained. The prosecution also proved that the value of 5 khthas of land in the name of Mohsenara Goni at Sector-10, Uttara although was shown at Taka 25,00,000, but PW 33 Nurul Islam Howlader by the oral evidence proved that he paid Taka 30,00,000 for the said land and thus he suppressed Taka 5 lac in the 'wealth statement, which was also beyond his legal source of income. The prosecution also proved keeping of Taka 15,000 in the savings account of United Commercial Bank, Barisal and Taka 25 lac in their joint names in Agrani Bank, Ray Shaheb Bazar Branch by the oral evidence PW 46 Md Abdul Hai, OW 54 SM Akhtar Hamid Bhuyan and PW 29 Md Abdus Samad and also by Exhibit-23 and Material Exhibit-XII. Taka 22,62,778.88 kept in the Standard Chartered Bank, Dhanmondi branch in their joint names was proved by the evidence of PW 43 and PW 54 and also by Material Exhibits-XIV and XV . The amount of Taka 20 lac in the name of accused Mohsenara Goni in Royer Bazar Branch of Agrani Bank was proved by the evidence PW 20 and by Material Exhibit-VIII Fixed deposit of Taka 20 lac in the name of Mohsenara Goni was proved by PW 22 and PW 23 and vide Material Exhibit-IX series. The appellant although in the wealth statement stated that they had fixed deposit of Taka 30,00,000 in their joint names, but during investigation Taka 41,11,500 was found in those accounts which has been proved by Material Exhibit-XIII and Exhibit-25.

<u>79. It further appears that the appellant was a Government servant and his wife was a simple housewife. The appellant joined the service in 1979 and during his tenure till 2007 he totally withdrew Taka 28,48,650.92 and paid tax by submitting returns. In the tax return submitted in 2006 (Material Exhibit-VI) he showed his total wealth of Taka 16,93,037/-. His wife Mohsenara Goni (absconding) was a housewife and she had shown her wealth in her tax file on account of ornaments, furniture, 50% of the land measuring 1762 sq. feet at Moneswar Road, 0.24 acres of land at Dakshin Khan and 3 kathas of land at Uttara from her father. But on consideration of the evidence it appears that the appellant had wealth of immovable property of Taka 13,12,500 and movable property of Taka 1,34,34,704, i.e., in total Taka 1,47,47,204+130 bhoris gold ornaments. On the other hand the movable and immovable property belonged to his wife was of Taka (1,36,52,729 + 1,05,64,448.41) = 2,42,17, 241.41 and in their joint names of taka 76,29,139.06+150 bhoris of gold. Totally they hold wealth of Taka 4,65,93,584.47+290 bhoris of gold, i.e., totally take 5,16,11,991.31 including gold. The appellant thus excluding his legal income illegally acquired wealth of Taka (5,16,11,991.31-19,30,527) = 4,96,81,464.31 which was beyond his legal source of income and his wife also abetted in acquiring and keeping the wealth in her name and possession. The appellant failed to make out a believable case by the evident of 2 DWs that the wealth in the name of his wife, was obtained from her father and other relatives. The above defense has been proved false by the evidence of prosecution witnesses. The appellant being a Government servant who withdrew fixed salary and had no paternal property of his own, as per income tax return, cannot be the owner and possessor of such huge wealth as found. The explanation given in the statement and the suggestions offered to the prosecution witnesses during cross-examination do not show that it was proportionate to his legal source of income, and, as such, the appellant committed the offence under section 27(1) of the Ain, 2004. In the above premises we hold that the prosecution witnesses by oral and documentary evidence successfully proved that the wealth acquired by the appellant was quite disproportionate to his legal and known source of income.</u>

<u>80. Let us see whether the property beyond the legal source of income should be confiscated. Most of the property of the appellant Osman Goni and in his wife's name found by the investigating officer and proved by the prosecution witnesses to be the property acquired by the appellant by illegal means beyond his known and legal sources of income. Convict Mohsenara Goni being a house wife cannot be the owner of the wealth as described and as found and proved by the witnesses, and, as such, the huge wealth which is beyond the legal source of income must be confiscated in favour of the state. So, the properties as described in the ordering portion of the impugned judgment, has rightly been confiscated by the Special Judge keeping out the properties from the list which proved to be acquired by his legal income. The trial Court confiscated the property relying on the evidence and materials on record, and, as such, we do not find any illegality in confiscation of the property.</u>

81. During trial, some vital witnesses, namely PWs 7, 15, 19, 20, 22, 23, 25, 26, 34, 44, 47 and 50 were not cross-examined by the defense without assigning any reason. Their evidence therefore, remained unchallenged and unshaken.

<u>82. The submission of the learned Counsel for the appellant relying on the case of 62 DLR (AD) 290/277 and 279 regarding he service of notice under section 26 of the Ain, 2004 upon appellant inside the jail and that the appellant did not get reasonable opportunity to respond to the notice and it was no notice in the eye of law, cannot be taken as a valid ground inasmuch by this time our Appellant Division in Criminal. Appeal Nos. 16-18 of 2013 heard along with Review Petition No. 18 of 2010 (yet unreported) has overruled its observation regarding service of notice inside the jail as made in the said case of 62 DLR (AD) 290.</u>

<u>83. It is mentioned here that the appellant in this case never took such plea that due to service of notice inside the jail, he failed to make a complete and proper wealth statement. He also did not take any steps during the trial to file any additional statement to supplement the original one. Moreover, the appellant was given enough time to submit his wealth statement and he submitted it after 14 (fourteen) days of the service of notice. In the above premises the submission of Mr. Ahmed has no leg to stand.</u>

84. In view of the discussion made hereinabove, we find no merit in the appeal and accordingly the appeal is dismissed. The judgment and order of conviction and sentence of the appellant Osman Goni and confiscation of the movable and immovable property of the spouse by the Special Judge in the aforesaid case is hereby affirmed.
